title: Tavi's Clever Corners
markdown:
The sun burst through Tavi’s window, bold stripes on the workshop floor. “Today is Kite Day!” She bounced. Pebble, her scruffy puppy, yipped and whirled around her feet. Spectacular flying. Brilliant blue skies.

She zoomed to the workshop: shiny wood, spools of colourful string, clever tools. Weeks on a kite frame for the town festival. She held it up. Floppy. Wobbly.

“Hmm.” She tapped a strut. Pebble nudged her hand with a cool wet nose. She pushed the frame straight; it flopped the other way, a sleepy kitten. A shivery tremor. This would not fly.

She sat on her stool. Pebble tumbled after a dust bunny, a fluffy heap. Tavi’s eyes found the workbench. Sturdy legs. Corners where the wood joined: strong, sharp. Her kite’s corners were not sharp. Floppy. A lazy puppy of a frame.

A butterfly passed the open window. She remembered Mr. Reed the carpenter talking about shapes that hold air, like a strong sail. The kite’s cross-struts were meant to meet in a big X. She peered. How did they meet?

“The bench legs stay steady because the corners are sharp — tiny triangles. Mine are floppy.” Favourite ruler. Sharp pencil. Measure. Adjust. Tighten. Pebble’s head tilted, ears perked. She pushed two pieces to meet at a different spot. Click. A sharper point. A determined angle. Again. Again. Each corner more solid. The wobble left. Balanced.

“Clever corners. When they’re right, the whole thing is steady.” She held the frame up. A little wooden soldier.

She dashed to the kite shop, chose brilliant blue — summer-sky cloth — taped it to the strong frame, added a long swishy tail of red ribbons.

Soon they trotted the highest hill, wind whistling. The kite tugged. Tavi ran. Pebble barked. It did not wobble. It did not flop. Whoosh — a brilliant blue bird against the clear sky.

“It’s flying!” Pebble chased imaginary butterflies.

Mr. Reed walked over, booming laugh, and left the my-dear off. “So steady. How?”

“The angles. Corners just right. Like strong triangles. Shape, and the wind.” She tugged; the kite dipped a graceful answer.

She did not declare they would win the festival or that the adventure was beginning. She let out a little more string and watched the tail write red commas on the blue. Pebble sat on her foot, which was as close as a puppy came to taking notes on corners.
